_comment: BEHAVIOURAL parity pin for token-lint's comment-state tracker (#3337).
token_lint_rules.json makes the four PATTERNS one artifact, and
tokenLintRuleParity.test.ts asserts the TS copies are byte-identical to it. But
deciding which text on a line is CODE is consumer LOGIC, not a pattern — it lives
twice, once per language:
- web/src/design/tokenLintRule.ts  `stripComments`
- personalclaw/apps/quality.py     `strip_comments`
A regex can be shared as data; a lexer cannot. So the BEHAVIOUR is shared as data
instead: every case below is run by BOTH sides' tests, and a case that reds in one
language and passes in the other is a parity break — the same two-dialect defect
the rules file exists to prevent, one layer up.
Each case is a whole synthetic FILE (`lines`), because the defect is cross-line by
nature. `expected` is one entry per line: the violation kinds the rail must report
for that line, in the order hex-then-px. `end_state` is 'code' or 'block' at EOF and
is the load-bearing control: a tracker that leaves block state stuck open reads as
'the rest of the file is clean' and silently stops catching real raw hexes, which
is the ONE way this change could weaken the rail rather than fix it. That is not a
hypothetical: tracking template literals as a third state leaked exactly this way on
three corpus files carrying a backtick inside a regex literal, which is why backticks
are not a state and why that case is pinned below.
Both directions are represented on purpose. Cases named `red_*` MUST still be
caught (the rail's value); cases named `clean_*` MUST now pass (the bug fixed).
Do not delete a `red_*` case to make a tracker change green — that is the
weakening this file exists to block.

cases.name: clean_interior_line_of_a_multiline_jsx_comment
cases.why: The reported defect. SkillInspector.tsx:65's shape: the issue reference sits on an interior line that carries no comment marker of its own.
lines: {/* Which surface this is: the inspector for a
not the list row — the row only summarises. */}

cases.name: clean_interior_line_of_a_ts_block_comment
cases.why: Same shape in a .ts file with a bare /* … */ rather than JSX braces.
lines: /* Routing note, see #3324 and #532 for the
prior attempts; #1783 is the live one. */

cases.name: clean_jsdoc_continuation_lines
cases.why: A `*`-prefixed continuation line is inside a block, not merely `*`-shaped. The old rule matched the SHAPE; this must hold on state.

cases.name: red_raw_hex_on_a_line_of_real_code
cases.why: Positive control, the base case. If this ever goes clean the rail is worthless.

cases.name: red_raw_hex_on_code_that_FOLLOWS_a_closed_block_comment
cases.why: The specific way a tracker breaks: block state left stuck open after `*/` makes every later line read clean. This case is the one that catches it.

cases.name: red_trailing_code_after_a_block_comment_closed_on_the_SAME_line
cases.why: Edge case, decided deliberately: the comment is stripped and the CODE after it is still linted. Anything else would make `/* … */ const c = '#abc'` a free bypass.

cases.name: red_trailing_block_comment_after_real_code
cases.why: The mirror: code first, comment second. The code half must still red and the comment half must not add a second hit.

cases.name: clean_line_comment_containing_a_block_terminator
cases.why: `app/swPolicy.ts` and `ui/SystemWidget.tsx` shapes: a `//` comment quoting `/*` or `*/`. `//` must win, or the tracker opens a block that never closes.
lines: // the bare comment `/* keep the draft */` cited #1783
// and `*/` alone must not close anything

cases.name: clean_string_literal_containing_a_block_opener
cases.why: `ui/widget/editMode.ts` ships exactly this. A string-unaware tracker treats it as a comment opener and swallows the rest of the file.

cases.name: red_hex_inside_a_string_is_still_a_violation
cases.why: Strings are not comments. Stripping comments must not start excusing string content — that is where every raw colour actually lives.

cases.name: red_hex_inside_a_multiline_template_literal
cases.why: A backtick is an ordinary character, so template CONTENT stays linted across lines: a css-in-template hex is a real violation and the strict direction is to keep catching it.

cases.name: clean_line_comment_inside_an_embedded_js_template
cases.why: `ui/widget/widgetSrcdoc.ts` and `pages/tools/ToolOutput.tsx` ship multi-line templates of embedded JS whose lines start with `//` and cite issue numbers. A line whose first non-space chars are `//` is prose in any non-block state.
lines: // the widget never learns why. Measured twice (#2263), months apart

cases.name: clean_backtick_inside_a_regex_literal_does_not_desync
cases.why: MEASURED: three corpus files carry one — `pages/chat/parseAssistant.ts` (`[\s(`'"]`), `pages/tools/ToolOutput.tsx` and `ui/content/renderers.tsx` (both /^```/m). Tracking template state desynchronised on exactly these and leaked block state to EOF. Telling a regex literal from a division needs real parser context, so backticks are simply not a state.

cases.name: clean_escaped_quote_does_not_close_the_string
cases.why: A tracker that closes on an escaped quote desynchronises and starts stripping real code as comment.

cases.name: red_nested_jsx_comment_braces_close_at_the_FIRST_terminator
cases.why: JS block comments do not nest, so `{/* {/* */} */}` closes at the first `*/` and the tail is code. Stated rather than assumed: the corpus has no nested shape, and pinning it keeps the two languages from inventing different answers.

cases.name: end_state_block_when_a_comment_never_closes
cases.why: The control's own control. An unterminated `/*` genuinely comments out the rest of the file, so reporting clean lines is CORRECT here — what must not be silent is the state, and `end_state` is how a caller sees it.

cases.name: end_state_block_survives_a_line_comment_it_contains
cases.why: Inside a block, `//` has no meaning. A tracker that honours it there would resume linting mid-comment and re-create the bug one line lower.
